title: Add cohort drift detector and backfill pipeline with CI gate
author: Aisha Khan
description: Introduce a lightweight statistical cohort drift detector and a one-off backfill pipeline, plus a CI gate integration that fails builds when an immediate, high-confidence drift is detected for critical prompt cohorts. Motivation: teams have seen occasional sudden regressions tied to prompt-set composition changes; this change provides an automated early-warning and a reproducible backfill path to diagnose root cause. The detector computes cohort-level distributions for generation-quality signals (token_precision, completion_coverage, and a normalized score) and evaluates divergence using both symmetric KL and a rank-based Mann-Whitney U p-value. We add configurable thresholds and minimum-sample safeguards; the default config uses cohort_kl > 0.12 OR mwu_pvalue < 0.01 with min_samples=200 to trigger a warning and an elevated threshold to fail CI (used only for protected prompt sets). The backfill pipeline can be invoked ad-hoc or scheduled; it uses batched inference with cache rehydration and writes cohort summaries to a new analytics table. The PR includes tooling to re-run historic evals against pinned model versions, a SQL migration to store cohort drift history, and docs for interpreting outputs and tuning thresholds. CI integration runs a fast sample-level check on pull requests for changed prompt sets and fails only when failure-mode thresholds are reached. Fallbacks: CI gate is opt-in per repo via eval-gates.yml and defaults to warn-only for most prompt sets to avoid blocking developer velocity. Performance: the detector adds negligible runtime to full evals (~+2% CPU) and backfill job processes 150k prompt-examples in ~7 minutes on the standard runner. This change is covered by unit, integration, and perf tests and includes examples and troubleshooting notes.

review_conversation: Initial implementation posted as a draft; reviewers asked for reproducible seeds and clearer minimum-sample behavior. Miguel requested that the fail gate be opt-in and warned about false positives on low-volume prompt cohorts; author updated config to be opt-in per repo and added warn-only default. Priya asked for performance numbers and an integration test that runs a mocked backfill; those were added. Evan requested a concrete troubleshooting doc; a new architecture page and FAQ were added. After two rounds of small fixes (deterministic seeding, error handling for empty cohorts), reviewers approved and marked as ready. Final merge performed via squash with conventional commit summary.
release_notes: Added cohort drift detection with configurable CI gating and a backfill pipeline for historic evaluation. New metrics (cohort_kl, mwu_pvalue) and a persisted drift history table enable trending and alerting. CI gate is opt-in and defaults to warn-only for non-protected prompt sets.
testing_summary: Unit tests for detector math and edge cases added; integration test simulates a backfill run against a small dataset using a mocked runtime, CI fast-sample check exercised in workflow; perf benchmark verified 150k samples processed in ~7 minutes on standard runner. All tests pass locally and on CI.
rollout_plan: Start as opt-in for a subset of protected prompt sets (10% of repositories) for 2 weeks, then expand to 30% and monitor false positive rate and signal-to-noise; full rollout gated on false-positive rate < 0.5% over a 14-day window. Backfill jobs run during off-peak hours by default (02:00 UTC).
performance_impact: Detector adds ~2% CPU overhead to full evals; storage for drift history table estimated at 8KB per cohort per day; backfill job processed 150k prompts in 7 minutes on the standard runner in our benchmarks.
notes: This PR targets improving early detection of prompt-set regressions and provides reproducible tooling to investigate and mitigate. Teams should opt in protected prompt sets into eval-gates.yml and tune thresholds based on historical variance.
